_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Gabon covering early Bantu and Pygmy peoples, Fang migration, Orungu and Mpongwe coastal trading states, French colonisation, Albert Schweitzer at Lambaréné, the Bongo dynasty (Omar 42 years, Ali 14 years), oil wealth, and the 2023 coup ending the Bongo dynasty.

ethnic_groups.name: Fang
ethnic_groups.notes: Bantu; northern and central Gabon; largest single group; Woleu-Ntem, Ogooué-Ivindo provinces

ethnic_groups.name: Mpongwe
ethnic_groups.notes: Coastal Bantu; Libreville area; historically dominant in trade with Europeans; first largely urban group

ethnic_groups.name: Nzebi/Bandzabi
ethnic_groups.notes: South-central; Ngounié province; part of larger Teke-Mbete cultural zone

ethnic_groups.name: Mbede
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern Gabon; Haut-Ogooué; related to broader Teke peoples

ethnic_groups.name: Punu
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern Gabon; Ngounié province; known for white-faced Okuyi masks

ethnic_groups.name: Teke
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern plateau; cross-border with Congo-Brazzaville; Teke kingdom heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Myene/Orungu
ethnic_groups.notes: Coastal cluster including Orungu, Galwa, Enenga; historical middlemen in slave trade

ethnic_groups.name: Kota
ethnic_groups.notes: Northeast; Ogooué-Ivindo; famous for brass-covered reliquary figures

ethnic_groups.name: Pygmy (Baka, Babongo, Bakoya)
ethnic_groups.notes: Forest hunter-gatherers; among oldest inhabitants; marginalized communities

ethnic_groups.name: Other (including European/Lebanese)
ethnic_groups.notes: French expatriates, Lebanese traders, other African migrants

natural_resources.notes: Oil backbone of economy since 1960s; world's #2 manganese producer (after South Africa, Moanda mine largest globally); timber exports (okoumé wood); Bélinga iron ore (massive deposit, Chinese interest, environmental controversy); 88% forest cover (one of most forested globally)

military.notes: August 2023 military coup ended Bongo dynasty (55 years, Ali Bongo ousted); General Brice Oligui Nguema transitional leader; French military presence (largest base in Gulf of Guinea); small but equipped forces; Republican Guard historically protected Bongo family

infrastructure.notes: Trans-Gabon railway key infrastructure; rivers used for transport.

climate_environment.notes: 13 national parks created 2002 (one of Africa's most ambitious conservation programs); 88% forest cover; carbon-positive country; Lopé National Park UNESCO; rainforest elephants, gorillas

debt_aid.notes: Oil wealth created upper-middle-income status but benefits concentrated; Bongo family wealth estimated $1B+; IMF Extended Fund Facility; post-coup transition government reforming

education.notes: French-language instruction; free public education; relatively well-funded compared to region; students also study in France/Morocco; small population means limited scale; oil wealth enabled significant education investment

diaspora_migration.notes: Small diaspora relative to oil wealth; French connections strong; immigration hub (workers from Cameroon, Congo, West Africa); Albert Schweitzer hospital legacy at Lambaréné drew international attention

digital_economy.notes: Relatively high internet penetration for Central Africa; submarine cables (SAT3/WASC/ACE); oil sector IT spending significant; limited startup ecosystem; e-government improving post-coup reforms

country_profile.notes_unique: Over 80% of the country is covered by tropical rainforest; the Lopé-Okanda landscape is a UNESCO World Heritage Site blending dense forest and savanna.

geography.terrain: Narrow coastal plains; hilly interior; savanna in east and south; 85% rainforest cover
geography.notes: Straddles equator; 85-89% rainforest cover; 13 national parks (11% of territory); Lopé UNESCO site.

economy_extended.notes: Oil-dependent (40% GDP, 80% exports); manganese (2nd global producer); timber; diversification strategy post-oil; Aug 2023 military coup ended Bongo dynasty (55 years).

health.notes: Albert Schweitzer Hospital (Lambaréné) historic; relatively high hospital bed ratio; malaria endemic.

food_agriculture.notes: Imports 60% of food; GRAINE programme to develop agriculture; abundant rainfall but minimal farming tradition.

energy.notes: Major oil producer; Grand Poubara hydroelectric dam (160MW); natural gas flaring reduction; oil reserves declining.

transport.notes: Trans-Gabon railway (Libreville-Franceville, 650km); limited road network; river transport important.

unesco_sites_list: Ecosystem and Relict Cultural Landscape of Lopé-Okanda
tourism.notes: 13 national parks; surfing hippos of Loango iconic; eco-tourism potential largely untapped; gorilla and elephant tracking.

human_rights_gender.notes: Aug 2023 military coup; Bongo dynasty ended; decriminalized homosexuality in 2020; women's rights improving but domestic violence concern.

security_stability.notes: Aug 2023 coup (CTRI) toppled Ali Bongo; transitional government under Gen. Oligui Nguema; ECCAS suspended membership.

cultural_heritage.media_landscape: State-dominated; some private media; RTG state; Gabon 24 news
cultural_heritage.notes: Fang masks influential in Western modern art (Picasso); Bwiti iboga ceremonies; Albert Schweitzer's hospital.

legal_system.notes: New constitution drafted after Aug 2023 coup; transitional charter; previously 1991 constitution.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: One of richest per capita in Africa thanks to oil.

current_leader.name: Brice Oligui Nguema
current_leader.title: Transitional President
current_leader.notes: Led military coup deposing Ali Bongo; cousin of the Bongo family; promised democratic transition

prime_minister.name: Raymond Ndong Sima
prime_minister.notes: Former opposition leader; previously PM under Omar Bongo 2012–2014

former_leaders.name: Léon M'ba
former_leaders.notes: First president; Fang leader; restored by French military after 1964 coup

former_leaders.name: Omar Bongo Ondimba
former_leaders.notes: 42 years in power; world's longest-serving president at death; converted to Islam; renamed country 'Gabonese Republic'; oil wealth and La Françafrique ties

former_leaders.name: Ali Bongo Ondimba
former_leaders.notes: Son of Omar; disputed elections 2009, 2016, 2023; health crisis 2018–2019; deposed by military August 2023
